description: Generate a clean ecomap (ecological map, Hartman style) for social work, family therapy, case management and school counselling: the client or household in a solid centre circle with its members listed inside, and 2–12 system circles around it (school, work, extended family, church, health care, probation, friends…), each joined to the centre by a line whose style shows the relationship: strong (thick line), moderate (plain line, the default), tenuous (dashed) or stressful (hatched red line). Arrowheads show the flow of energy or resources: to the system, from it, or both ways. Each system may carry a short detail outside its circle, and a legend of the line styles sits underneath. Choose it to map a person's or family's relationships with outside systems; use a hub and spoke for neutral parts around a centre with no relationship quality, a mind map when the items branch further, and an org chart for reporting lines. Limits: 2–12 systems, 0–8 household members, system names of 1–3 words, details of about 10 words. Use first names or roles only; never put identifying client details in the chart. Infer missing details rather than asking; the user can adjust the chart in the builder through the Edit link. ALWAYS give the user the image link: inline chat images usually cannot be saved, but the link renders the exact chart on demand and can be pasted into a slide or Markdown.

inputSchema.description: An ecomap (Hartman style): a client or household in the centre, the systems around them, and lines whose style shows the strength of each relationship and arrows for the flow of energy or resources.

center.description: The client or household in the middle: a solid circle in the first palette colour with the name in bold white and the members listed under it, e.g. { "name": "Lopez household", "members": ["Maria, 34", "Leo, 9"] }. Use first names, roles or ages only.

color.description: Optional hex colour of the centre circle. Default: the first palette colour (indigo #4f46e5); the systems take the following palette colours.

members.description: Optional household members listed small inside the centre circle, one per line (0–8), e.g. ["Maria, 34", "Leo, 9"]. A first name or role with an age reads best; the circle grows to fit.

name.description: Name of the client or household, e.g. "Lopez household" or "Sam". Bold white text, wrapped to up to 2 lines.

credit.description: Shows a small "twominutetoolkit.com" credit under the chart, inside the card. Set false to leave it off (for example when the user asks for no branding).

legend.description: Show the legend under the map explaining the four line styles and the arrows. Default true; set false when the audience already knows the notation.

palette.description: Hex colours applied in order to items that have no colour of their own. Pass the user's brand colours here when they name them. Default: indigo, sky, emerald, amber, red, gray.

systems.description: The systems around the centre (2–12), placed clockwise from 12 o'clock: people, groups and services such as School, Work, Extended family, Church, Health care, Friends, Probation, Benefits. One system still renders but is reported as a warning; more than 12 are dropped.

color.description: Hex colour of this system's circle, e.g. "#10b981". Optional: systems without one take the next palette colour.

detail.description: Optional short note shown outside the circle, on the side away from the centre, wrapped to up to 3 lines (about 10 words), e.g. "Weekly visits from grandma".

flow.description: Direction of energy, support or resources along the line: "none" (default, no arrowheads), "to" (from the client to this system), "from" (from this system to the client) or "both" (a two-way exchange).

name.description: System label inside its circle, 1–3 words reads best (e.g. "Extended family"). Long names shrink and wrap to up to 3 lines.

strength.description: Quality of the relationship, drawn as the connecting line's style (Hartman's ecomap convention): "strong" (thick solid line), "moderate" (plain solid line, the default), "tenuous" (dashed line) or "stressful" (red line crossed by short hatch marks, -/-/-).

title.description: Heading shown top-left of the chart at 22px bold. Every chart has one title row; an empty string hides it.

width.description: Chart width in pixels (640–2400). Omit it (recommended) and the chart sizes itself to its content with comfortable margins, between 880 and 1280px wide. PNG output renders at 2x.
